  Contributing or Development section in README -- quality-gate commands
  always go in CONTRIBUTING.md"). It was also stale -- it listed `make
  check` as vet+staticcheck+markdownlint+tests, but the real `check`
  target (Makefile:54, post-#242) also runs golangci-lint and
  govulncheck. Quality-gate commands now live in the new CONTRIBUTING.md,
  linked from Documentation.
- Multi-line copy-paste command blocks split into one command per fence
  throughout (Quick Start's inspect/manual-install blocks, all of Setup's
  credential-setup alternatives) per the standard's code-block rule.
- Description trimmed from a ~40-line intro (How It Works prose, a
  numbered pipeline example with per-stage timings, a "Two types of
  commands" breakdown) to one paragraph, and rewritten to describe
  present reality rather than the larger vision as if it were shipped.

That last point is the substantive one, not just formatting: the old
Description described beadle-daemon's GPG-signed command-pipeline
mechanism (Claude + CLI runner stages composed like Unix pipes) as
something a user gets from the Quick Start install. It isn't --
beadle-daemon is dev-only source (`make build-daemon`, no CI test
coverage gate distinct from beadle-email's), never built by `make dist`
or release.yml, never installed by install.sh, never registered in
plugin.json. Confirmed against prfaq.tex's git history (last tracked at
fd6a8f0, before the #223 untrack) that this pipeline vision is exactly
what the PR/FAQ describes -- a September-2026-dated, hypothesis-stage
press release for a product that doesn't ship yet. The only artifact
released today is beadle-email (v0.16.5's GitHub release has exactly
four beadle-email binaries, no beadle-daemon). The rewritten Description
states this honestly: beadle-email is the first shipping piece of the
larger daemon vision, and that daemon isn't part of this release. Also
dropped a "beadle-daemon mission runner" aside from the CLI section's
scoping explanation for the same reason -- it isn't user-reachable.

no-passphrase signing-key state replaced with generic placeholders) --

the standard's guidance for that section.

Reordered sections to match the standard's required order: Title+Tagline
-> Badges -> Description -> Platforms -> Quick Start -> Features -> What
It Looks Like -> MCP Tools/Commands -> Setup -> project-specific sections
(Trust Model, Identity, Contact Permissions, CLI) -> Documentation ->
License. Documentation section now links CONTRIBUTING.md, as required
when a project has quality gates.
EOF
